forecast-period.text: A trough of low pressure over the far northeast will linger over the far northeast until mid week. A high pressure system in the Bight will move across southern parts of the state today, then out over the Tasman sea by Wednesday morning. A trough of low pressure approaches the western border on Wednesday then moves across the west and north of the State on Thursday and eastern parts on Friday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible showers and thunderstorms about the far north. Maximum temperatures below average, grading to above average in the far northeast and in the southwest. Southwest to southeasterly winds, tending east to northeasterly in the west.

Possible showers and thunderstorms developing about the west. Maximum temperatures near average, grading to above average about agricultural areas, and below average in the northwest. East to northeasterly winds, tending moderate to fresh and gusty northeast to northwesterly in the west ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change in the southwest later.

Showers and thunderstorms about the west and north, mostly likely in the north. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to below average in the northwest. Southeast to northeasterly winds, fresh and gusty at times in the north.

text.p: Showers and thunderstorms about the north and east. Maximum temperatures generally near average in the north and west, below average about the northwest and above average elsewhere. East to northeasterly winds in the east at first, with southwest to southeasterly winds extending throughout during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: Less than 2 mm across the agricultural areas, increasing to 1 to 5 mm about western, northern and eastern parts, increasing to 5 to 15 mm about the west and parts of the Pastoral districts, with local falls of 10 to 30 mm are possible with thunderstorms mostly about the north and west.
